proofs.full_local_argument: This is a local reconstruction, not a quotation or independent-review result. It uses the source's Theorems 2–3 and conjugate subgradient identity as stated mathematical inputs. Write s=L−μ>0, a_i=g_i−μx_i and b_i=<x_i,g_i>−f_i−μ||x_i||²/2. Those inputs imply that S is F_{μ,L}-interpolable iff there exists a proper closed (1/s)-strongly convex H with H(a_i)=b_i and x_i∈∂H(a_i) for every i: in the forward direction conjugate f−μ||x||²/2, and in the reverse direction take f=H*+μ||x||²/2. Fenchel equality gives exactly the stated b_i and restores f_i and g_i. Necessity for H follows by applying the subgradient inequality to H(z)−||z||²/(2s): b_i≥b_j+<x_j,a_i−a_j>+||a_i−a_j||²/(2s). Conversely assume these inequalities. Set H(z)=max_j{b_j+<x_j,z−a_j>+||z−a_j||²/(2s)}. This finite maximum is finite, continuous and (1/s)-strongly convex, because subtracting ||z||²/(2s) leaves a finite maximum of affine functions. At z=a_i every term is at most b_i and term i equals b_i; thus H(a_i)=b_i. Moreover H(z)≥b_i+<x_i,z−a_i>+||z−a_i||²/(2s)≥H(a_i)+<x_i,z−a_i>, so x_i∈∂H(a_i). The conjugate H* is finite everywhere: a quadratic lower bound on H makes <x,z>−H(z) bounded above for each fixed x. The source's conjugation and curvature-subtraction statements therefore give the required f and its interpolation data. To identify the condition explicitly, put Δx=x_i−x_j and Δg=g_i−g_j. Direct substitution yields b_i−b_j−<x_j,a_i−a_j>−||a_i−a_j||²/(2s)=f_j−f_i+<g_i,Δx>−μ||Δx||²/2−||Δg−μΔx||²/(2s). The last two terms combine to −[||Δg||²+μL||Δx||²−2μ<Δg,Δx>]/(2s). Hence nonnegativity is equation (4) for the ordered pair (j,i); requiring every ordered pair is exactly the displayed condition. Setting μ=0 gives Corollary 1. No Algorithm coverage or lower bound follows from this equivalence.

assumptions: I is finite and nonempty; d is a positive integer.
0≤μ<L<∞; all inner products and norms are Euclidean.
No distinctness of x_i is assumed; all ordered pairs, including coincident sites, must satisfy the condition.
statement.conclusion: For all i,j: f_i−f_j−<g_j,x_i−x_j> ≥ [L^{-1}||g_i−g_j||²+μ||x_i−x_j||²−2μL^{-1}<g_j−g_i,x_j−x_i>]/[2(1−μ/L)]. In particular, at μ=0 this is equivalent to f_i≥f_j+<g_j,x_i−x_j>+||g_i−g_j||²/(2L), the finite-L case of Corollary 1.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Use the Euclidean inner product and norm on R^d. In this finite-L restriction, F_{μ,L}(R^d) denotes differentiable convex functions on R^d with L-Lipschitz gradient and convex f(x)−μ||x||²/2. Data S={(x_i,g_i,f_i)}_{i∈I} have x_i,g_i∈R^d and f_i∈R. Interpolation means f(x_i)=f_i and ∇f(x_i)=g_i for every i.
statement.parameter_domains: d∈{1,2,...}; 1≤|I|<∞; μ∈[0,∞), L∈(μ,∞). This record deliberately restricts the source's broader extended-L convention to finite L.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such d,I,μ,L and data S, there exists a single f∈F_{μ,L}(R^d) interpolating every triple if and only if the displayed inequality holds for every ordered pair (i,j)∈I×I. There is no randomness.

summary: For finite Euclidean data and 0≤μ<L<∞, pairwise inequalities exactly characterize interpolation by an L-smooth μ-strongly convex function. This is a model-membership certificate, with no Oracle Complexity claim.
title: Smooth strongly convex interpolation: finite-L necessary and sufficient conditions
use_when: Check whether prescribed finite values and gradients can be realized by one smooth strongly convex function.
